children.title: What each site is serving
children.subtitle: Tap Refresh to read the live build stamp from each site. Same commit on both = dev and production are in sync. Different commits = dev is carrying work production does not have yet.

children.value: Both cards stay empty until you tap Refresh — this dashboard never shows a build stamp it did not just fetch from a live site. One site being unreachable leaves that card alone; it does not blank the other.

children.title: Read-only release dashboard
children.subtitle: The first slice of running the dev-to-production pipeline from inside isan.

children.value:
Production reads https://devisant.com/isa/build_info.json — the stamp the production deploy writes.

Dev reads https://dev.devisant.com/isa/build_info.json — the stamp the dev deploy writes.

Both are plain public JSON files ({build, commit, builtAt}). This applet only ever reads them. It holds no credentials, and it cannot deploy, promote, or change anything.

Each card's title is the short commit the site is serving. Same commit on both cards means dev and production are in sync. Different commits mean dev is ahead — it has landed work that has not been promoted to production yet.

A site's build stamp changes only when that site is deployed. Landing a commit on the dev BRANCH does not change the dev SITE until the dev site is published.

Caching: each site serves its build stamp with a ten-minute cache. A deploy finished seconds ago can take a few minutes to show up here. If a stamp looks behind, wait and refresh again.

Not shown yet: how many commits dev is ahead by, and whether CI is green. Both need authenticated access to a private repository, and this applet deliberately carries no credentials. They arrive in a later phase, served by the backend rather than fetched by the client.
